edition.en: The complete essay with its epigraphs, from Essays: First Series, Project Gutenberg eBook #2944, which follows the revised text of 1847.
edition.zh: 全文连同题词，据古登堡计划电子书 2944《随笔集第一辑》，该版依据 1847 年修订本。

basis.en: First published in 1841 and revised in 1847; Ralph Waldo Emerson died in 1882.
basis.zh: 1841 年初版，1847 年修订；爱默生卒于 1882 年。

note.en: Emerson’s 1841 essay, the source of “a foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds”. It is a sermon for trusting your own perception against the crowd, written with an aphorist’s compression and, sometimes, an aphorist’s overreach. Read it next to Schopenhauer on thinking for oneself, which makes a harder version of the same case. The Chinese gives the opening and the passages on doing your own work and on consistency.
note.zh: 爱默生 1841 年的文章，“愚蠢的一贯性是小心眼的妖怪”一语即出于此。它像一篇布道，劝人面对众人时相信自己的感知，写得有格言家的凝练，有时也有格言家的过头。可以与叔本华《论独立思考》对照着读，后者把同一个道理说得更硬。中文译出开头，以及论做自己的事、论一贯性的几段。

excerpt.orig: Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
excerpt.en: Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
excerpt.zh: 相信你自己：每一颗心都随着这根铁弦振动。
